title: THE FLAMINGO PARADE IS A MATING DISPLAY
caption: Why do greater flamingos dance in groups? 🦩 #Flamingo #Courtship #BirdBehavior #NatureFacts #WildVox

narration_timeline.text: Why do these greater flamingos march together and swing their heads like dancers?
narration_timeline.scene: Open on authentic greater flamingo courtship filmed in Camargue.

narration_timeline.text: During breeding season, birds gather and start moving in coordinated groups.
narration_timeline.scene: Show real Phoenicopterus roseus flock at lagoon; do not assert every shot depicts breeding.

narration_timeline.text: They stretch their necks, turn their heads, and step through shallow water.
narration_timeline.scene: Use flock movement or genuine display, never another flamingo species.

narration_timeline.text: These group displays help flamingos assess possible mates before forming pairs.
narration_timeline.scene: Show actual greater flamingo vocalizing/displaying; do not imply pair formation on camera.

narration_timeline.text: It looks like choreography, but these movements are part of a real courtship ritual.
narration_timeline.scene: Show a real group of greater flamingos in the water.

narration_timeline.text: That strange parade helps these long-legged birds find partners for breeding.
narration_timeline.scene: Close on greater flamingo flock, resolving the opening parade question.
